column2: the plan adds `scripts/test-cleanup-sessionstart.sh` and `scripts/test-cleanup-sessionstart.md` on the same makefile-only harness pattern as `scripts/test-sweep-design-logs.sh` / `.md`, but omits matching `agent-lint.toml` carve-outs. ci runs `agent-lint --pedantic`; g004/dead-script reachability does not follow makefile targets, so the new harness pair will likely be flagged and `make agent-lint` may fail on the pr.

the plan registers `scripts/cleanup-sessionstart.sh` in `hooks/hooks.json` for direct execution, but does not require mode `100755` or mirror the `test-sweep-design-logs.sh` executable precondition in the new harness. a committed `100644` file can pass listed harness cases while sessionstart fails with permission denied and the automatic age-based sweep never runs.

the plan preserves the `cache json: <path>` stdout line and skill/docs durable-cache contract while the proposed `finally` block removes `temp_root` before process exit on normal non-preserve paths. callers or wrappers that follow the printed path get a missing file immediately after a successful `/report-tokens analyze` run.

default cleanup deletes generated plot files on linux, or on macos when `larch_report_tokens_no_open` is set, despite printing their paths in stdout. the proposed `finally` removes `temp_root` before the operator can open advertised pngs, regressing the optional plotting feature.

planned `test_report_tokens_cli.py` coverage exercises empty scan, no-plot success, failure-before-post, and macos auto-open preserve, but not the main non-auto-open plot paths. a regression that preserves `temp_root` whenever `plot_paths` is nonempty (without the correct platform or `larch_report_tokens_no_open` guards) could re-leak top-level `larch-report-tokens.*` roots on linux/ci or macos with auto-open disabled while all planned tests stay green.
